release_summary.summary: Incorrect bill calculations due to recent changes to billing import validation rules cause wrong bills (even with actual meter reads) and drive the observed increase in dispute tickets. Symptoms: dispute ticket volume rose from ~610 in June to 1260 in September 2026 [E-04]; disputed bills contain more ACTUAL reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240) [E-01]. The increase in dispute volume is shown by monthly ticket counts [E-04]; the read-type distribution indicates disputes are not solely due to estimation [E-01]. AMI read events show high-consumption rejections linked to the import rule change [E-10], and hypothesis H-RULE-CHANGE is supported by these evidences [E-01, E-10]. The release implements monitoring of dispute ticket volume to track progress toward baseline. It does not include fixing the billing import validation rule change. The gate resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs, leading to a RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION decision. This is because the scope only monitors volume while evidence shows disputes are driven by rule‑change‑induced calculation errors, and the critical unknown U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S remains open. The release scope only monitors dispute ticket volume and does not fix the billing import validation rule change identified as the root cause. The approved rationale (monitoring volume) contradicts evidence that disputes are driven by rule‑change‑induced calculation errors, not volume alone, and the VOB for the exact faulty rule (VOB-U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S) is open and outside the release scope.
